mission.display_title: Derive Bayesian estimators from simple loss functions
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to use simple loss functions to derive Bayesian estimates of parameters. So the point summary is loss-justified.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force linking a named loss to a posterior summary (e.g. mean/median). Refuse arbitrary point picks.
mission.learning_objective: Use simple loss functions to derive Bayesian estimates of parameters.
mission.concept_focus: Loss function → Bayesian point estimator (mean / median) → refuse conflating with credible intervals.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday simple posteriors (5.1.3). Today summarises under loss.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to derive Bayesian point estimators from simple loss functions.
success_criteria: Closed-book, name one simple loss and the posterior summary it leads to.
State why the estimator depends on the loss.
Refuse picking a point estimate without loss warrant.
task_descriptions: Knowledge Checks: loss pair + refuse arbitrary pick.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name squared-error loss and absolute-error loss. Which posterior summaries do they typically lead to?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Squared-error → posterior mean; absolute-error → posterior median (as standard cases).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Posterior for θ is available. (1) Under squared-error loss, what Bayesian point estimator do you use, and under absolute-error loss? (2) Refuse: 'Just take the posterior mode always' and 'the Bayesian point estimator under loss is the same object as a credible interval.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Squared-error loss → posterior mean; absolute-error loss → posterior median. (2) Refuse default mode (the Bayesian point estimate should follow from an explicit loss. A point estimator summarises the posterior under a loss; a credible interval is a posterior probability set for θ) different objects.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Defaulting to the mode without a loss, or conflating a point estimator with a credible interval.
